body: Atoms can form molecules. In a covalent bond, a pair of atoms shares electrons. A water molecule consists of an oxygen atom covalently bonded to two hydrogen atoms. The atoms form a bent arrangement.

Chemical behavior depends on composition and arrangement. For example, carbon dioxide is linear and water is bent. Combined with differences in how different atoms attract shared electrons, geometry affects the distribution of electric charge and how a molecule interacts with its surroundings.

limitations: A ball-and-stick drawing is a geometrical model. The sticks and size of the spheres do not depict the detailed distribution of electrons.
purpose: Connect microscopic bonding to molecules and later material behavior.
